title: CVE-2026-109469: CVSS 10 Entra Device Registration Flaw
content_md: Microsoft has disclosed CVE-2026-109469, a critical elevation of privilege vulnerability in Entra Device Registration, the cloud service that registers and joins devices to Microsoft Entra ID. The flaw carries a maximum CVSS score, meaning that an unauthenticated attacker could exploit it over the network with no user interaction. Customers have nothing to patch. Microsoft says it has fully mitigated the issue in the service, lists it as neither exploited nor publicly disclosed, and rates exploitation as less likely. The CVE exists for transparency, and Microsoft has released almost no technical detail beyond the score and the weakness type. What Is CVE-2026-109469? Microsoft’s advisory describes CVE-2026-109469 (CVSS 10.0) as an authorization bypass through a user-controlled key in Entra Device Registration that allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network. The weakness maps to CWE-639 . In plain terms, that class covers services that accept an identifier supplied by the requester, such as an object or record ID, without checking that the requester is allowed to act on that object.
